description.narrative: The objective of the Education Improvement Project for Lesotho is to improve the quality of teaching and enhance the physical learning conditions in targeted primary and secondary schools. The project has three components. (1) Improving the quality of teaching in primary and secondary schools component has multiple sub-components: Strengthening teaching of foundational skills (literacy and numeracy) in early primary grades (Grades 1-3), Implementing a National Learning Assessment in junior secondary (Grade 9), Scaling up online mathematics and science training for junior secondary school teachers. (2) Enhancing physical learning conditions in primary and secondary schools component has the following sub-components: Improving basic infrastructure in targeted primary schools and constructing laboratories and workshops in targeted secondary schools. (3) Strengthening project management, and governance of education system component includes Supporting decentralization of the Teaching Service Department to districts and Project monitoring, evaluation, management, environment and social safeguards, procurement, financial management, and audit activities.

title.narrative: IRI 8: Newly built and furnished classrooms in targeted primary schools (by ecological zone)

comment.narrative: Construction commenced in February 2026 for 46 of the 52 primary schools in Batch 1, organized across 6 packages. Most contractors are on sites and are engaged in site establishment, excavation and clearance, material mobilization, and procurement of PPE. Efforts are ongoing for the commencement of construction for the remaining 6 schools in batch 1 and all schools in Batch 2, 3, and 4. The retendering of the remaining 6 primary schools was conducted alongside the 31 secondary schools under Batch 2 between November 2025 and mid-January 2026. Bid evaluation for the 37 schools has been completed, with contract awards concluded by April 22, 2026. For Batch 3 (63 primary schools), contract commencement is estimated for August 2026, while Batch 4 (17 secondary schools) is expected to commence in September 2026.

comment.narrative: Significant preparatory steps have been completed since the last ISR. A Training of Trainers workshop was conducted, with 66 Master Trainers trained on the newly developed FLN curriculum materials. Stakeholder sensitisation was completed on February, reaching 30 key stakeholders including District Resource Teachers, Inspectors, NCDC, and NTTs. A total of 40 teachers from 40 pilot schools have been trained on the Grade 1 FLN curriculum packages. New teacher materials are currently being printed for dissemination to 300 selected schools, with suppliers selected and the printing process underway; dissemination to schools has not yet been completed While these activities indicate that implementation is progressing as planned, verified data on the number of primary school students directly benefitting from improved foundational learning is not yet available. An updated and verified count will be reported in the next ISR.

title.narrative: PDO Indicator 1: Primary school students benefitting from improved foundational learning (by gender), Cumulative

comment.narrative: Significant progress has been made towards achieving this PDO indicator. The curriculum for Grades 1, 2, and 3 has been comprehensively updated and is currently awaiting digitalization. The pilot implementation of the new curriculum is scheduled to commence as schools reopen in early 2026. In preparation, teacher training on the revised curriculum is planned for January 2026 to ensure effective delivery and uptake. The digitalization process will begin with uploading the curriculum materials, starting in December 2025 and concluding by March 2026. At present, the baseline for this PDO indicator is set at zero, as the updated curriculum has not yet been implemented in schools. This baseline accurately reflects the current status, where no students or teachers have yet benefited from the new curriculum. Monitoring of the curriculum's impact on foundational learning outcomes will be conducted as implementation progresses, allowing for a robust assessment of its benefits once rollout begin

title.narrative: IRI 1: Foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN) curriculum and instructional materials for Grades 1-3 reviewed, digitized, and adapted to be gender responsive and contextually relevant.

comment.narrative: The National Curriculum Development Centre (NCDC) has developed the early grade Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) curriculum, and the digitalization of Grade 1 numeracy materials is completed. Efforts are ongoing to digitalize the remaining teaching and learning materials for the new FLN and also to make instructional materials gender responsive. Adaptation of the curriculum has not yet commenced; however, this process is anticipated to occur concurrently with the curriculum rollout. Formal engagement with the NUL Centre for Teaching and Learning is yet to be initiated; the Ministry is currently reviewing modalities for accelerating the digitization process, including potential external partnerships, and is expected to outline a clear engagement and acceleration plan by July 15, 2026.

title.narrative: IRI 1: Foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN) curriculum and instructional materials for Grades 1-3 reviewed, digitized, and adapted to be gender responsive and contextually relevant.

comment.narrative: The foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN) curriculum and instructional materials for Grades 1-3 have undergone review. Digitization of these materials is planned for completion by March 2026. Efforts are ongoing to ensure that the curriculum and instructional materials are gender responsive. Adaptation of the curriculum has not yet commenced; however, this process is anticipated to occur concurrently with curriculum rollout.

IRI 4: Secondary school teachers in targeted schools certified in provision of content knowledge and pedagogical skills for teaching mathematics and science (by gender, ecological Zone)

comment.narrative: Baseline (222) is from BESP records, but is not disaggregated by gender or ecological zone, may include teachers outside LEIP-targeted schools, and certification standards may differ from those under LEIP. It is recommended to disaggregate the baseline, verify certification criteria, align the baseline to LEIP schools, and establish ongoing data collection for accuracy. The endline target should be revised upwards to reflect new certifications supported by LEIP.

title.narrative: IRI 4: Secondary school teachers in targeted schools certified in provision of content knowledge and pedagogical skills for teaching mathematics and science (by gender, ecological Zone)

comment.narrative: The number of secondary school teachers in targeted schools certified in the provision of content knowledge and pedagogical skills for teaching mathematics and science remains zero because the online training will begin later this year. There are significant efforts to achieve this goal. In February, the evaluation of technical and financial proposals submitted by National University of Lesotho (NUL) and Lesotho College of Education (LCE) was completed and contract negotiations finalized during the current mission. Admission lists for in-service teacher trainees were finalized by the Ministry of Education and Training and are undergoing verification. Learner registration on Learning Management System (LMS) platforms and teacher orientation are scheduled for completion by June and July 2026, respectively, while procurement of equipment is ongoing.
